title: Cain and Abel

lettering_types.caption: Narration box
lettering_types.divine: God's words: Cinzel on solid dark band, no speaker drawn

world_rule: Setting rule for Genesis 4: open land east of Eden; fields, flocks and simple stone or earth works only; no cities, no buildings.

panels.camera: medium, warm light, the woman holding a newborn wrapped in hide, the man beside her
panels.art: Eve holding her first son, Adam looking on.

text.text: The man knew Eve his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Cain, and said,
I have gotten a man with Yahweh’s help.
text.speaker: EVE

panels.camera: wide split composition: a grown farmer breaking soil on the left, a grown shepherd with his flock on the right
panels.art: Cain tilling a field; Abel keeping sheep on a hillside.

text.text: Again she gave birth, to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

pages.layout: large top panel, two bottom panels

panels.camera: wide, two brothers on an open hill at evening, each presenting an offering
panels.art: Cain bringing grain and fruit; Abel bringing a firstborn lamb.

text.text: As time passed, Cain brought an offering to Yahweh from the fruit of the ground.
Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat.

panels.camera: close, warm light falling on the younger brother and his offering

text.text: Yahweh respected Abel and his offering,

panels.camera: close, the older brother's face in shadow, angry, eyes down

text.text: but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell.

panels.camera: medium, Cain alone on the hill at dusk, turned away

text.text: Yahweh said to Cain,
Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen?

panels.camera: low, a dark doorway of a rough stone shelter with deep shadow at the threshold, Cain small beyond it

text.text: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.

panels.camera: medium, the two brothers side by side, Cain speaking

text.text: Cain said to Abel, his brother,
Let’s go into the field.
text.speaker: CAIN

panels.camera: extreme wide, two tiny distant silhouettes in a field under a darkening red sky, one rising over the other; nothing graphic, no weapon, no blood
panels.art: The field at dusk, far away.

text.text: While they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, and killed him.

panels.camera: medium, Cain alone in the field at dawn, defiant

text.text: Yahweh said to Cain,
Where is Abel, your brother?
He said,
I don’t know. Am I my brother’s keeper?
text.speaker: CAIN

panels.camera: close on the bare earth of the field, a fallen shepherd's staff in the grass; no blood visible

text.text: Yahweh said,
What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.

pages.layout: large top panel, two bottom panels

panels.camera: wide, cracked dry ground stretching to the horizon, Cain small and kneeling

text.text: Now you are cursed because of the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

panels.camera: close, Cain's hands in barren soil

text.text: From now on, when you till the ground, it won’t yield its strength to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.
Cain said to Yahweh,
My punishment is greater than I can bear.
text.speaker: CAIN

panels.camera: medium, Cain standing in a beam of light; nothing drawn on his body
panels.art: Cain under a shaft of light.

text.text: Yahweh appointed a sign for Cain, so that anyone finding him would not strike him.

panels.camera: extreme wide, a lone figure walking east into a barren land, seen from behind

text.text: Cain left Yahweh’s presence, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

panels.camera: medium, warm light, Eve holding a newborn wrapped in hide, Adam beside her; the baby's face hidden
panels.art: Eve with her newborn son Seth.

text.text: Adam knew his wife again. She gave birth to a son, and named him Seth, saying,
for God has given me another child instead of Abel, for Cain killed him.
text.speaker: EVE

panels.camera: wide, a small gathering of people on a hillside at dawn, hands lifted, among them a grown man holding an infant
panels.art: People beginning to call on Yahweh's name.

text.text: A son was also born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. At that time men began to call on Yahweh’s name.

moral.heading: What This Story Teaches
moral.paragraph: Two brothers brought offerings, and God respected Abel’s. The Bible later explains why: “By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain” (Hebrews 11:4). God warned Cain before he sinned: “sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it” (Genesis 4:7). Cain did not listen, and anger became murder. The apostle John uses this story to teach a simple command: “we should love one another” (1 John 3:11), “unlike Cain” (1 John 3:12). Even after this sorrow, God gave Adam and Eve another son, Seth, and people “began to call on Yahweh’s name” (Genesis 4:26).
